slides.title: Sharing is dividing
slides.text: A sack of plums lands on the workbench and four friends are waiting. Sharing it fairly, so everyone gets the same, is division.

slides.title: Two sharing questions
slides.text: Division answers two questions. If you know the number of groups, find the share: 12 plums shared by 4 friends is 3 each. If you know the share, find the groups: 12 plums in bags of 3 fill 4 bags.

visual.label: Two bars of 12 plums: shared by 4 friends, each share unknown; packed in bags of 3, the bags counted

rows.label: Share 12 by 4 friends: how many each?
Pack 12 in bags of 3: how many bags?

focus.cue: Know the groups (4 friends): find the share. 12 ÷ 4 = 3 each.
Know the share (3 a bag): count the groups. 12 ÷ 3 = 4 bags.

slides.title: Rough first, then share
slides.text: Rough first: 29 plums shared by 4 friends is about 7 each. Share them out one by one and see what is left.

visual.label: 29 plums shared by 4: 4 rows of 7, 1 left over

focus.cue: One row for each friend: 7 plums each.
After fair shares of 7, 1 plum is left over.

slides.title: Leftovers need a decision
slides.text: A remainder is not a mistake. It is a leftover that needs a decision: one more van, a shared last slice, or a plum saved for later.

slides.title: Stretch: Big shares
slides.text: Long sharing works in chunks. For 96 shared by 4, share 80 first (20 each), then 16 (4 each). Each share is 24.

visual.label: Sharing 96 by 4 in two chunks: 80 first, then 16, so each share is 24

focus.cue: Share 80 first: each of the 4 shares gets 20.
Then share 16: 4 more each. Each share is 20 + 4 = 24.

words.means: splitting an amount into equal shares or groups
one equal part that each person or group gets
what is left over after equal sharing
the answer to a division: how many in each share

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Sum Racer. It opens on the Volcano Valley track, division questions only, and it stays there. Win the race: picture the fair shares before you answer.
slides.alt: Sum Racer's Volcano Valley track on a phone: question 2, a sharing (division) fact, four answers to pick from.
